headline: What shall we
grow for tea?
lead: Start with something you love eating. A row of peas to shell on the way back from the plot, perhaps, or a few beetroot to roast while they’re still small and sweet.
blurb: Each crop has a pair of illustrated pages. You can choose a variety, check when to sow and see how far apart to plant, all with the seed packet still in your hand. And if the slugs get to your lettuces first, there’s practical advice on protecting the next row.
authorNote: John Lennon has grown food organically for over 30 years. He shares his garden in Cornwall on YouTube at @hackriculture.
season: When the last potatoes are lifted, the chapters on compost and crop rotation will help you plan what goes in their place.
